title: ShapleyFL: Robust Federated Learning Based on Shapley Value

problem.claim: Federated learning must train a robust global model despite invisible, heterogeneous, corrupted, or malicious client data and updates, while also managing communication and computation costs.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies a need for a federated learning algorithm that improves robustness while addressing communication and server computation costs.

contributions.claim: A Shapley value-inspired adaptive weighting mechanism models federated learning as sequential cooperative games and adjusts client weights according to client contributions.
An importance-sampling client strategy reduces communication cost by optimizing the variance of global updates according to client weights.
A client-weight calculation method estimates differences between clients' Shapley values to reduce server computation cost.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on several real data sets demonstrate the effectiveness of their approaches.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated learning enables collaborative global-model training without sharing clients' local data.
Robust global-model training is difficult because client data are hidden, heterogeneous, potentially corrupted, or malicious, and practical algorithms face communication and computation costs.
The proposed approach uses Shapley-inspired adaptive client weighting based on sequential cooperative-game contributions.
Importance sampling reduces communication cost, while estimating Shapley-value differences reduces server computation cost.
Experiments on several real data sets are reported to demonstrate effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Client weights are adjusted according to estimated client contributions.

interpretation.claim: Contribution-aware weighting may provide a mechanism for improving robustness when client updates differ in reliability.

application.claim: In distributed training, consider contribution-aware weighting together with sampling and computation-cost controls.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish performance across particular attack types, heterogeneity regimes, or deployment settings.

unknowns: Specific data sets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
The threat model, robustness guarantees, and behavior under particular corruption or attack patterns are unspecified.
Algorithmic details and computational or communication cost measurements are omitted.
